_source: Plainly Difficult (1.1M subs), Kolkata flyover collapse, 628K views, 9:39. Built-in browser 2026-11-20: frames at 0/6/22 s, sampled moments 150, 260, 275, 330, 348, 355, 372, 440, 495, 500 s and the last 20 s; transcript panel counted (1,560 words, ~164 wpm; never copied). SAMPLED. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: stock footage of a jammed Kolkata street full of yellow taxis
hook.firstLine: City planners everywhere struggle to keep traffic moving.

shots.picture: stock footage, crowded street with yellow taxis, buses, hand carts
channel wordmark in white rounded type over the same footage
stock footage of Indian highways and city traffic, long holds
search-result and document screenshots for the cost figures over a dimmed money photo
flat 2D construction site: grey deck and piers, yellow digger, blue bus, gritty charcoal sky; stick-figure mascot bottom-right
top-down satellite photo of the route through dense rooftops
flat 2D side elevation: a concrete truck tipping its load onto the deck, traffic below
real CCTV of the span falling onto cars
aftermath photos: broken girders, rescuers, diggers
flat 2D: the collapsed deck lying across the road, hi-vis workers
flat 2D joint diagram on chalkboard texture: cantilever girders hinge down off the pier as the load arrives
the channel's cause scorecard: a grid of failure causes, the ones that applied stamped with yellow circles

lines.gist: why moving traffic through an old dense city is so hard
years of delay end in a sudden collapse onto the road
names the flyover and the city; chapter one closes
planning, contract, cost and the builder's troubles
delays, cut corners and the rush to finish
the day: concrete pouring, the span falls, the rescue
the inquiry: the joint could not carry the load; who signed off
asks which causes the viewer agrees with

ending.cta: comment which causes you agree with

whyItWorks: The failure is explained on a flat side-elevation diagram where the exact part moves (girders hinging at the pier) as it is named.
A recurring signature ending: a cause scorecard stamped per video, which invites comments.
Six named chapters; real footage of the collapse is held back to ~60% of the runtime.
Voice only: no music under the narration, full silence between sentences.
